entities.name: Fadrique Enríquez de Velasco
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fadrique Enríquez de Velasco II (1460–1538), 4th Admiral of Castile and Lord of Medina de Rioseco, stood as a towering figure in the consolidation of early modern Spain under the Catholic Monarchs and Emperor Charles V. His military prowess, particularly during the critical Revolt of the Comuneros (1520–1522), proved instrumental in suppressing Castilian noble and urban dissent, thereby solidifying monarchical authority and shaping the trajectory of the burgeoning Spanish Empire. His lineage, wealth, and strategic command made him a linchpin in the transition from late medieval feudal structures to a more centralized imperial state, influencing the political stability of the Iberian Peninsula for decades.

As the hereditary Admiral of Castile, Fadrique Enríquez commanded significant naval and military resources, deploying them effectively against the comunero forces. His most decisive intervention occurred at the Battle of Villalar on April 23, 1521, where, alongside Íñigo Fernández de Velasco, the Constable of Castile, he led the royalist army to a crushing victory over the comunero rebels, capturing their leaders Juan de Padilla, Juan Bravo, and Francisco Maldonado. This triumph effectively dismantled the comunero resistance, which had sought to limit royal power, protect traditional Castilian liberties, and prevent foreign influence in the court of the young Charles V. Beyond Villalar, Enríquez participated in subsequent campaigns to quell remaining pockets of rebellion, ensuring the complete pacification of Castile by 1522.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fadrique Enríquez de Velasco's decisive military actions, particularly at the Battle of Villalar, were critical in suppressing the Revolt of the Comuneros, thereby solidifying Habsburg monarchical power in Spain and enabling the crown to leverage Castilian resources for its nascent global empire.
